title: [WT-05] Wrappers: launch every CLI inside the task worktree with per-worktree configs
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.1 and §5.2 (configs, agents copy, grok trust; the links are WT-06).

Objective: in worktree mode the agent CLI edits W, never the control checkout, while still reaching the daemon through the control checkout.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- cwd = W for claude, codex (exec -C W), gemini and grok (--cwd W). In ps1 that means Push-Location W for EVERY CLI, including the claude launch that today runs in the launcher's cwd.
- MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control checkout. Export MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET from the claim's workspace. The proxy path stays the one resolved from the wrapper's own location.
- Run the existing per-CLI config writers with W as the config root: W/.mcp.json (sh) or the ps1 temp --mcp-config (an interactive sh seat passes --mcp-config W/.mcp.json); W/.codex/config.toml; W/.gemini/settings.json; W/.grok/config.toml plus the grok trust grant for W.
- Copy <control>/.moe/agents/*.md into W/.claude/agents/.
- A config write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, calls report_blocked and launches no CLI.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-04 (task-c20464ff64ca49fca4371dd9b5194364).

NOT in scope: Serena root, the skills and memories links, the deps notice (WT-06); landing (WT-07 onward); shared-mode launches, which must stay byte-identical; docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses, fake CLI that records its cwd and env): in worktree mode the CLI's cwd is W, MOE_PROJECT_PATH is the control checkout, and MOE_WORKTREE_PATH / MOE_TASK_BRANCH / MOE_LAND_TARGET match the claim's workspace.

postflight case: the per-CLI config lands in W (W/.mcp.json or the ps1 temp config, W/.codex/config.toml, W/.gemini/settings.json, W/.grok/config.toml) and the control checkout's copies are not rewritten.
postflight case: W/.claude/agents/*.md equals <control>/.moe/agents/*.md; a forced config-write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and launches no CLI.
postflight: every existing shared-mode launch case passes unchanged.
Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes (grep -oE diff over moe-agent.sh vs moe-agent.ps1 is empty).
The verification command exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes via node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell.

Add: 1. cli mode: when WT_CLI_RECORD is set, also append one JSON line to that file: {cwd: process.cwd(), argv: process.argv.slice(3), env: MOE_PROJECT_PATH, MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET (null when unset), mcpConfig: the text of the file named after --mcp-config, else null}. An argv containing --version prints `0.0.0-fake` and records nothing. 2. Per-type shims named claude, codex, gemini and grok, each in its own directory under the suite root. The wrappers take the CLI type from the --command basename with the extension stripped. sh: `exec "" "" cli "$@"`. ps1: `.cmd` running `"" "" cli %*`, then `exit /b %errorlevel%`. Model both on the existing shim. 3. launch() takes an optional trailing options object {type, args}: type picks the shim, args are appended to the wrapper argv. Without it, launch() behaves as before. 4. The fixture's control gets an untracked .moe/agents/x.md. enableAgentTeams keeps its default, true. Cases. Each uses a fresh fixture with FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE for task-postflight, MOE_DISABLE_ARGV_PROBE=1, WT_CLI_RECORD=/record.jsonl and GROK_HOME=/grok-home. W is the workspace path, and same(a,b) compares fs.realpathSync.native of both sides, lower-cased on win32. launch-claude, launch-codex (--codex-exec / -CodexExec), launch-gemini (--gemini-exec / -GeminiExec) and launch-grok (--grok-exec / -GrokExec), as one loop. Assert: (a) Exit 0 and exactly one record. claude, gemini and grok record a cwd that is same() as W. codex's argv has -C followed by W (its working root), and grok's has --cwd followed by W. (b) MOE_PROJECT_PATH is same() as the control; MOE_WORKTREE_PATH is same() as W; MOE_TASK_BRANCH === 'moe/task/task-postflight'; MOE_LAND_TARGET === 'main'. (c) W holds the CLI's configs, each naming the control as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH: - sh: W/.mcp.json for every type (JSON mcpServers.moe.env.MOE_PROJECT_PATH); - W/.codex/config.toml or W/.grok/config.toml (the `MOE_PROJECT_PATH = "…"` line, its value JSON-decoded); - W/.gemini/settings.json (JSON); - ps1 claude: the record's mcpConfig, its temp --mcp-config. codex also gets W/.codex/agent-instructions.md, and gemini W/.gemini/GEMINI.md. (d) "Not rewritten", by banner count. For each writer banner the type prints, count log lines ` `. With backslashes read as slashes, a path ending in /.worktrees/task-postflight/ is W; any other path ending in / is the control. Expect exactly 1 each, or 2 each for the sh Gemini banner, which that writer prints twice per write. The banners are sh `Wrote project MCP config:` (every type) and, on both, `Codex MCP config written to:`, `Gemini MCP config written to:` and `Grok MCP config written to:`. Match the whole banner: ps1's claude line `MCP config written to:` is a suffix of the others. (e) W/.claude/agents holds exactly the .md names in /.moe/agents, each byte-equal (Buffer.equals). grok: /trusted_folders.toml has a [folders.'

'] header with same(p, W). config-fail (codex): before the launch, make W the way WT-04T's half-made case does (`worktree add --lock --reason "moe task-postflight" --no-checkout --no-track -b moe/task/task-postflight W main`). sh wrapper, part 1, in scripts/moe-agent.sh: the writers become functions, plus the per-task worktree phase.

Save rule for EVERY moe-agent.sh save in steps 2-3:
- Never patch the live file in place. Running bash seats read it at stale offsets (mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse, task-f31d415d).
- Build the whole new file as a copy on the SAME filesystem, e.g. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/c4cccb84/moe-agent.sh, and run `bash -n` on it.
- Check that the live file's sha256 is unchanged since you copied it, then make ONE `mv -f` onto scripts/moe-agent.sh.

1. Wrap the writers in place. Do not re-indent their bodies.
   - ensure_mcp_config's tail, from `    # Also write project-level .mcp.json`, becomes `write_project_mcp_json ROOT SERENA_PROJECT`, which writes ROOT/.mcp.json. ensure_mcp_config ends by calling it with "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT".
   - The codex (~916), gemini (~1089) and grok (~1284) blocks become write_codex_config, write_gemini_config and write_grok_config. In each:
     - the `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = … ]; then` line becomes the function header plus `local root="$1" SERENA_PROJECT="$2"`. The local shadows the global, so the body's Serena references need no edit;
     - the block's closing `fi` becomes `}`;
     - right after the function, the old site becomes `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = codex ]; then write_codex_config "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT" || exit 1; fi`, and the same for gemini and grok.
   - In the bodies only the file location moves. `$PROJECT/.<cli>` and `$PROJECT/.mcp.json` become `$root/…`, and grok's `grant_grok_folder_trust "$PROJECT"` takes "$root". The value written as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays "$PROJECT", the control, whatever ROOT is. `exit 1` becomes `return 1`.
   - Error handling: bash ignores set -e inside a function run from an `||` list. So add `|| return 1` to each body's mkdir and to its python heredoc command (`… << 'PYEOF' || return 1`). Otherwise a failed write over an existing file passes the `[ -f ]` check. Keep that check as well.
   - Keep the comment line `# For grok: write project-scoped .grok/config.toml (same [mcp_servers.*] TOML` verbatim. prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs ends its codex_moe_server_override slice there.
2. Per-iteration reset, beside `    MOE_TOP=""` (~6633), where WT-04 resets MOE_WT_*: `CLI_ROOT=""; unset MOE_WORKTREE_PATH MOE_TASK_BRANCH MOE_LAND_TARGET`. An empty CLI_ROOT means shared mode.
3. Define `prepare_worktree_launch` next to WT-04's provision_worktree. It does three things:
   - Sets CLI_ROOT="$MOE_WT_PATH" and exports MOE_WORKTREE_PATH="$MOE_WT_PATH", MOE_TASK_BRANCH="$MOE_WT_BRANCH" and MOE_LAND_TARGET="$MOE_WT_TARGET" (the claim's bare target).
   - Writes into CLI_ROOT what the pre-flight writes into the control for this CLI: write_project_mcp_json, then the CLI's own writer when CLI_TYPE is codex, gemini or grok. The grok writer grants grok folder trust for W.
   - Under the pre-flight agents mirror's gate (`"$ENABLE_AGENT_TEAMS" = true` and `$MOE_DIR/agents` present), runs `mkdir -p "$CLI_ROOT/.claude/agents"` and copies every `$MOE_DIR/agents/*.md` there with `cp -f`. Loop with a `[ -f ]` guard; an agents dir with no .md files is not a failure.
   Follow every writer, mkdir and cp with `|| worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED "<what> (<path>)"`. That is WT-04's refusal: it prints `[ERROR] CODE: detail`, calls report_blocked once, launches no CLI and exits 1. Call it directly, never inside $(...), a pipeline or a subshell. Nothing falls back to the control.
   The writers already read an exported MOE_DAEMON_HOST. Confirm it is exported by this point, so W's TOML needs no extra upsert.
   WT-06 will insert its Serena root and link step at the top of this function, before the writes. Leave no placeholder line.
4. Call it with `if [ "${MOE_WT_MODE:-}" = worktree ]; then prepare_worktree_launch; fi` directly after the `fi` that closes the `preflight_landing … launch` block (~7666), above `    # Compose final PROMPT`. comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
@architect-bc59d28a WT-04's planner here. Your plan builds on WT-04 (task-c20464ff, rev 1). Its contract:
- Provisioned values: sh sets MOE_WT_MODE (worktree or shared), MOE_WT_PATH (W), MOE_WT_BRANCH and MOE_WT_TARGET, only after a successful provision. ps1 sets $script:MoeWtMode, MoeWtPath, MoeWtBranch and MoeWtTarget. W is derived from the seat's own git top. It is never taken from the claim's workspace.path, which a Windows daemon spells D:\.
- Seat-stopping refusal: worktree_stop CODE DETAIL (sh) / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat -Code -Detail (ps1). It prints `[ERROR] CODE: detail`, calls report_blocked once and exits 1. Route your failed config write through it with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- Tests: the held-out suite is scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs (WT-04T, task-dd5daa4b), which both harnesses run. Add your cwd/env cases there. The fake-proxy knobs are FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE, FAKE_CTX_WORKSPACE and FAKE_CTX_COMMITS.
- DoD 5: WT-04 renames moe-agent.sh's nine MOE_LAND_* env-bridge names to MOE_PY_*, so the codes diff starts empty. Any MOE_LAND_TARGET export you add must appear in both twins, comments included.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When WT-04 provisioned the seat in worktree mode (sh MOE_WT_MODE / ps1 $script:MoeWtMode = worktree), a worker seat launches every CLI against W: claude, gemini and grok run with cwd W, codex gets -C W and grok --cwd W. Before the launch, the per-task phase (sh prepare_worktree_launch, ps1 Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch) writes into W the per-CLI configs the pre-flight writes into the control: sh W/.mcp.json for every CLI plus the CLI's own config; ps1 the CLI's own config, with claude on the existing temp --mcp-config. All of them name the control checkout as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH. The phase also copies <control>/.moe/agents/*.md into W/.claude/agents, grants grok folder trust for W, and exports MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET from WT-04's values. MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control. A failed W write is refused through WT-04's worktree_stop / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED: one report_blocked, no CLI, exit 1. Shared mode is byte-identical to HEAD.
acceptanceCriteria: postflight-worktree.cjs cases launch-claude, launch-codex, launch-gemini and launch-grok pass under both harnesses. claude, gemini and grok run with process cwd W; codex gets -C <W> and grok --cwd <W>. MOE_PROJECT_PATH is the control, and MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET equal W, moe/task/task-postflight and main.

W holds the CLI's configs: sh W/.mcp.json for every CLI, plus W/.codex/config.toml, W/.gemini/settings.json or W/.grok/config.toml; ps1 claude keeps its temp --mcp-config. Each names the control as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH. Each writer banner names the control exactly once and W exactly once (twice each for the sh Gemini banner).

W/.claude/agents/*.md is byte-identical to <control>/.moe/agents/*.md, and grok's trusted_folders.toml trusts W. config-fail refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED through WT-04's refusal path: one report_blocked row, no CLI, exit 1.
Every existing postflight case and every WT-04T case passes unchanged, and the two wrappers' MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_ code sets are equal.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Copying the writers for W: rejected, because two definitions per CLI would drift. Each writer is wrapped in place, and the shared pre-flight calls it with the control.
2. cwd = control with --add-dir W: rejected by design §5.
3. New postflight.{sh,ps1} blocks (revision 1): replaced by WT-04T's shared suite, which both harnesses already run.
4. Calling the phase inside WT-04's provisioning `if`: rejected. That `if` sits inside the taskless-handoff slices, and under the ps1 slice's EAP Stop an undefined function fails the render. The calls sit after the landing/baseline block instead.
5. sh `cd W` in the main shell: rejected, because post-flight and the EXIT trap would then run git in W. The launches cd inside their subshells, and codex uses -C.
6. Passing the exported MOE_WORKTREE_PATH as the trust step's launchDir: rejected, because the lease test inherits the agent env. The trust step uses the unexported CLI_ROOT.
7. A per-task ps1 claude --mcp-config: deferred to WT-06. The DoD allows the temp config.
